artifacts.title: Psiaki v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Mr. Psiaki complained that Covenant Presbyterian Church's Session erred in installing officers elected at a congregational meeting that excluded communicant members under age 18 from voting, in violation of the BCO. The SJC sustained the complaint (15-5), holding that all communicant members have a constitutional right to vote in officer elections regardless of age, and that church bylaws may not override BCO provisions; multiple dissenting opinions argued that BCO 20-3 and 24-3's phrase 'good and regular standing' permits local sessions to establish reasonable minimum voting ages.

artifacts.synopsis: Seven members of a PCA mission church were tried and censured by a provisional Session for opposing the organizing minister's continuation as permanent pastor. The SJC sustained the appeal and reversed the convictions, holding that the indictments lacked required specificity under BCO 32-5, that the accused had no sinned against the fifth or ninth commandment by expressing opinions about ministerial suitability, and that the right to choose a pastor belongs to the congregation—not the provisional Session. A concurring opinion addressed indictment requirements, standard of review in appeals, and congregational rights in mission church minister selection.

artifacts.synopsis: RE Reese and TE Bech complained that Philadelphia Presbytery erred in declaring their complaint out of order after Presbytery refused to allow any questions of TE Jason Hsu regarding his views on women deacons when approving his transfer to City Line Church. The SJC sustained the complaint, finding that deeming parts of a complaint objectionable is insufficient grounds to rule the whole complaint out of order, though it agreed the proposed amends (removing TE Hsu) were not appropriate.

artifacts.title: Appointing unordained men and women to diaconal ministry roles

matches.evidence: CCB found an overture appointing unordained persons to diaconal ministry in conflict with the Constitution, including because it implied an unordained office contrary to BCO 17-1.
